correctness.rationale: The cubic edge count gives 2k=10+e(X)+c for any deletion leaving a nonempty forest, hence k>=6. At size six there are 14 surviving vertices and 12+e(X) surviving edges, so acyclicity is equivalent to having exactly 2-e(X) components. An independent exhaustive calculation used this component-count test on all 38,760 masks, tested state-pair symmetric differences and base adjacency directly, and obtained exact shortest-path layers by bitset frontiers from every state. It reproduces both frozen metric distributions on all 4,088,370 unordered pairs, 2,860 states, 27,780/8,280 edges and eccentricity distributions {6:2860}/{9:520,10:2340}. The surcharge histogram agrees in all seven bins; all 210 maximum pairs have (overlap,jump,slide)=(4,2,8). The Johnson excess maxima and frequencies are 2 on 840 pairs and 6 on 240 pairs. Each move in both displayed witness paths is valid and each path is shortest. The independent check includes these joint and path assertions, rather than inferring them from marginal histograms or presuming the frozen scripts explicitly assert them.
residual_risks: Exact finite classification for this one base graph, not a general reconfiguration theorem.

value.rationale: The canonical cubic incidence graph is a natural common test case for arbitrary exchanges versus local mobility under minimum cycle-breaking constraints. The exact cost separation includes pairs only two jumps apart but eight slides apart, distinguishes the locality cost from the Johnson lower-bound gap, and gives a reproducible reference for constrained shortest-path algorithms. This is information not provided by the known optimum count alone.
residual_risks: Benchmark for one graph, not evidence of the same costs for other graph families.
